# flowstate

> Think out loud. Ship in text. flowstate is an open-source speech-to-text CLI
> with a bundled local web UI. It captures your voice, transcribes it with Groq
> Whisper, cleans the text with an LLM pass, and writes the result to stdout,
> the clipboard, the focused app, or the browser. One Go binary, on macOS,
> Linux, and Windows.

## What it is

- A terminal-native, pipe-friendly dictation CLI: `flowstate`.
- A bundled local web UI started with `flowstate web` (default 127.0.0.1:8585).
- The same Go binary, config file, and Groq API key power both interfaces.

## How it works

1. Capture audio (in-process for the CLI, in-browser for the web UI).
2. Transcribe via Groq Whisper.
3. Clean up via a Groq LLM pass that removes filler, fixes punctuation, honors
   self-corrections, preserves domain spellings, and leaves code and command
   names intact.
4. Output to stdout, clipboard, paste into the focused app, or the browser
   (page + history + JSON/Markdown export).

## Install

    go install github.com/mazen160/flowstate/cmd/flowstate@latest

You bring your own Groq API key via the GROQ_API_KEY environment variable. The
project is free and MIT licensed; the only cost is Groq usage.

## Privacy

The CLI writes only to the destinations you choose. The web server never
persists audio or transcripts; history lives in the browser's localStorage and
audio streams straight to Groq without touching disk on the server.

## How it compares

- vs Superwhisper: Superwhisper is Mac only with a local model; flowstate is
  cross-platform and bring-your-own-key.
- vs Wispr Flow: Wispr Flow is a subscription with a proprietary model and no
  CLI; flowstate is free, terminal-native, and scriptable.
